S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder involves the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor, occurring within months of the event and causing marked distress or functional impairment beyond what would be expected. Clinically, it often presents with mood changes, anxiety, or maladaptive behaviors tied closely in time and content to specific life events such as relationship conflict, health changes, or occupational stress. The course is typically time-limited, with symptoms resolving within six months after the stressor or its consequences end, though it can persist if the stressor is ongoing. It is distinguished from normal stress reactions by the degree of impairment and from other disorders (e.g., major depression, PTSD) by its less severe, more situationally bound presentation and the absence of defining features such as full depressive episodes or trauma-related re-experiencing.

patient.stressor: About six months ago, Thomas had to shut down his small handyman side business after losing a major contracting opportunity due to licensing and insurance paperwork he had procrastinated, which also led to a dispute with a long-time client over unfinished work. Around the same time, his chronic back pain worsened, making it harder to take on heavier jobs and pushing him fully out of the workforce just as his family was counting on his income to cover rising living costs and his daughter’s community college tuition. Over the next five months, he found himself increasingly stuck between guilt over not contributing financially and avoidance of the administrative steps needed to restart in a more formal way, spending more time alone on the river or in his workshop but leaving projects half-organized and ignoring calls from former customers. His wife finally pressed him to see a mental health professional after he began backing out of club activities and community volunteer commitments, telling her he felt like he no longer knew how to respond to the pressure of getting his work life back on track.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like I’ve shut down and keep reacting badly ever since my work fell apart, and I can’t seem to handle anything that reminds me of getting back into business.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Ever since the business fell apart, any time my wife brings up paperwork or a customer leaves a voicemail, I just kind of shut down—I get this mix of dread and shame, my mind goes blank, and I end up hiding in the garage or taking off to the river instead of dealing with it, even though I know I’m just making things worse.

add_requirements.onset_within_3_months_of_stressor: Within a few weeks of losing that big contract and realizing I had to shut down the handyman work, I started freezing up anytime I had to deal with business stuff and just couldn’t bring myself to return calls or tackle the paperwork.
add_requirements.time_limited_course: I feel like this shutdown has been tied directly to my work falling apart—before that I could juggle things okay, and I keep thinking that if I could just get the business side sorted out again, this whole spiral would probably ease up.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because of all this, I’ve basically stopped taking any new jobs, let my old customers drift away, pulled back from my club and volunteer work, and now my wife is stressed because we’re short on money and I’m not really pulling my weight at home or in the community.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about five months now, ever since the side business collapsed and my back pain got bad enough that I stopped working altogether.
